outcomes.text: Analyze computing problems using computing and other relevant disciplines.
Develop and evaluate computing solutions against stated requirements.
Make professional computing decisions informed by law and ethics.
Contribute to and lead teams working in the discipline.
Apply AI methods with awareness of their assumptions, societal impacts and stakeholder needs.

requirements.title: Application elective
requirements.summary: Choose one listed course carrying 3–4 credits, or two listed courses carrying 1.5 credits each. Individual credits are not supplied in this pool; the two selection routes must not be conflated.

requirements.title: University degree GPA and residency
requirements.summary: CWRU cumulative GPA must be at least 2.000. Earn at least 60 CWRU credit hours, including 15 after reaching 105 total credits. At least half of all major requirements, including required related-field courses and major electives, must be completed in CWRU courses.

requirements.title: Catalog choice and extended study
requirements.summary: Use matriculation requirements or elect a later Bulletin. Beyond ten years, the department may update the major and the Associate Provost may update unfinished general education after reviewing the academic record.

requirements.title: BA school requirements
requirements.summary: Earn at least 120 total credit hours, including 90 in arts and sciences and 30 at the 300/400 level. Arts/sciences includes College of Arts and Sciences courses and biochemistry, computer/data sciences, economics, neuroscience and nutrition. Concurrent BA+BS students are exempt from six of the 90 arts/sciences hours. The cumulative average for graded major courses must be at least 2.000.

requirements.title: Unified General Education Requirements
requirements.summary: Applies to matriculants from 2023–2024; earlier cohorts can elect a later Bulletin. A course may fulfill every requirement for which it is approved, except that a cross-listed course counts in only one breadth area. Pools are the complete published Bulletin inventory; later approvals may be added during the year.

requirements.title: Breadth outside AI: arts/humanities and social sciences/management
requirements.summary: AI is classified STEM+N. Earn at least 18 credits with passing letter grades in A+H and SS+M, at least six in each. Up to nine may use approved tests/transfer; at least three credits in each area must be taken at CWRU. Incoming transfer students may receive additional approved pre-matriculation transfer breadth credit. One cross-listed course may count toward only one breadth area.

requirements.title: Arts & Humanities eligibility
requirements.summary: Eligible published departments/subjects: Art History and Art (ARTH, ARTS); Bioethics (BETH) undergraduate courses; Classics (AKKD, ANEE, CLSC, GREK, HIER, LATN); Dance (DANC); English (ENGL, WRIT); History (HSTY); Humanities (HUMN); Modern Languages and Literatures (ARAB, CHIN, FRCH, GRMN, HBRW, ITAL, JAPN, KORE, LING, PORT, RUSN, SPAN); Music (MUED [ except MUED 320 ], MUGN, MUHI, MUTH); Philosophy (PHIL); Religious Studies (RLGN); Theater (THTR). Additional approved identifiers (slash-linked listings are cross-listed choices, not multiple required courses): BIOL 233, EDUC 301, ENGL 267, JWST 267, WLIT 267, JWST 310, WLIT 310, JWST 380, WLIT 380, JWST 381, WGST 381, WLIT 381, WLIT 382. Department-wide eligibility remains an open rule.

requirements.title: Social Sciences & Management eligibility
requirements.summary: Eligible published departments/subjects: Anthropology (ANTH); Cognitive Science (COGS); Political Science (POSC); Psychological Sciences (PSCL, COSI); Sociology (SOCI); All courses offered by the Weatherhead School of Management (ACCT, BAFI, BLAW, DESN, ECON, ENTP, MGMT, MIDS, MKMR, OPMT, OPRE, ORBH, PLCY, VEAL). Additional approved identifiers (slash-linked listings are cross-listed choices, not multiple required courses): CHIN 350, CHIN 350D, ECIV 110, EDUC 304, EDUC 336, EEPS 207, ESTD 101, GRMN 314, NTRN 310, NTRN 340, NTRN 350, NTRN 351, PHIL 222, PHIL 392, SJUS 100. Department-wide eligibility remains an open rule.

requirements.title: Communication sequence and Experience Portfolio
requirements.summary: Pass with letter grades an Academic Inquiry Seminar in the first or second semester, two communication-intensive courses of at least three credits each, disciplinary communication of at least three credits, and a capstone of at least three credits. Submit work from every component to the Experience Portfolio, including inquiry and capstone reflections. DC/capstone may be approved sequences and are usually completed within the major.

requirements.title: Wellness enrollment duration
requirements.summary: Pass with letter grades two semester-equivalents of wellness, with at least one semester-equivalent involving significant physical movement, regardless of course credits. Combine full/half semesters. A repeatable course counts for at most one semester or two half-semesters, except varsity sports, ROTC and marching band. Formal transcripted enrollment is required; active military service waives the requirement. Approved transfer credit is permitted.

requirements.title: Inquiry seminar placement and transfer
requirements.summary: Choose AIQS 100, 110, 120 or community-engaged AIQS 130 (four credits). Students needing academic-English preparation take AIAE 100 (three credits) first, then the seminar; others enter AIQS 120 directly. Incoming transfers who completed prior first-year writing receive inquiry transfer credit. Other students require FSCUE appeal approval to use transfer credit. Submit two inquiry assignments; the printed word counts are ordinary examples, not universal numeric minima.

requirements.title: Communication residency and portfolio
requirements.summary: Both communication-intensive courses and disciplinary communication must be taken at CWRU; test/transfer substitution requires FSCUE appeal approval. Capstone must be taken at CWRU. Upload one assignment per communication-intensive course and a disciplinary communication artifact; capstone includes final project/public-facing explanation and final reflection. The portfolio also includes synthesis and self-assessment.

requirements.title: Quantitative and perspectives credit policies
requirements.summary: Quantitative reasoning requires a passing letter grade in an approved course of at least three credits; approved test and transfer credit may satisfy it. Moral/ethical reasoning, global perspectives, and human diversity each require passing letter grades in an approved course or sequence. Local/global engagement permits passing an approved course/sequence or participating in an approved activity. Transfer substitution for any perspective requires FSCUE appeal approval.

requirements.title: Secondary-major relationship
requirements.summary: This record represents the full AI degree. Students completing AI only as a secondary major within another undergraduate degree are exempt from this AI degree's school-specific requirements under the published program policy.

notes: Complete is a reviewed degree-scope inventory of the cited 2026–2027 major, university degree page and Unified General Education Requirements, not an automated graduation certification. Open department-wide courses, SAGES capstone designations and approved substitutions are represented as approval rules rather than falsely finite lists.

UGER permits approved overlap with major/minor/breadth. Course options are not additive new degree credits: CSDS 310 is listed for disciplinary communication and CSDS 395A for capstone; programming options CSDS 132/134 are listed for quantitative reasoning. One cross-listed course counts in only one breadth area.

Where an existing major course had null credits, a matching UGER code/title row supplies its numeric credit-hour observation; source case-unified-general-education supplies this additional metadata provenance. The original course identity source remains the major catalog.

UGER wellness zero-credit courses are explicit published zeros and still count by enrollment duration. Multi-course sequence totals do not become individual credits. Published title/code pools may overlap, so inventory counts are neither required-course totals nor unique university-wide courses.

2026-10-11 correctness hotfix: exact CSDS core descriptions correct programming/data structures/algorithms to computing foundations and Discrete Mathematics to mathematics; ENGR 399 in the BS is human context. Category reviews are independent from requirement membership. Programming remains an alternative between CSDS 134 and the CSDS 132+237 bundle; prerequisites are metadata, not new fixed course obligations. The wider degree taxonomy remains unreviewed; the separate degree correctness audit is in progress, not certified by existing inventory completeness.

2026-10-11 major-course audit: all named major course descriptions read. Prerequisites are course access conditions, not additional fixed degree requirements. Source-stated Units are not converted to semester hours without separate evidence. CSDS 102 requires no current or previous 300-level CSDS enrollment; CSDS 499 permits graduate standing OR Requisites Not Met permission; other advanced courses retain their own prerequisites or permissions. CSDS 463 heading and degree row agree, but its description cross-list footer says CSDS 466; no alias or equivalence inferred.

Application options SCMG 462 and SCMG 463 are listed by the BA, but current course descriptions require enrollment in the Master of Supply Chain Management program. No undergraduate exception is stated in the reviewed degree or course sources; option eligibility is unresolved.
